utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you all. I open the hearing. Mr. Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Case Number IT-95-9-A, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Simic, can you follow in a language that you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would the parties identify themselves, please. May we have the appearances and let's start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Mr. Mathias Marcussen, and our case manager is Ms. Sue Grogan. For the purpose of the Status Conference, Mr. Marcussen will be dealing with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Farrell. May we have the appearances for the Defence of Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. My name is Igor Pantelic, lawyer from Belgrade, and I represent Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. We are here for a Status Conference. Let me remind you that pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal that we're going to hold a Status Conference, which is to be held within 120 days of the appeal. And then 120 days afterwards to allow the person to be allowed to appeal. The appeal was filed by Mr. Simic on the 17th of November. And it was the -- it is the first Status Conference, in actual fact, to be held in this case. Having said that, we are holding a Status Conference in order to allow the appellant to raise any queries he might have with respect to his conditions of detention or with regard to his health, both physical and mental. Mr. Simic, or rather, Mr. Pantelic, do you have any matters to raise with respect to matters of that type?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, personally I am not in a situation to give any particular details regarding the personal state, physical and mental state of my client. Of course he will be able to give more details. On behalf of my Defence team, I would like to just inform you and for the record that my learned friend from the Prosecution and me, we got one conference, short conference, before this hearing regarding the relations of disclosure, and some issues regarding the form of material which might be provided to Defence by the Prosecution in accordance with Rule 68. So maybe later on also my learned friend can give you more information with that regard. But as far as Dr. Simic's status is concerned, I don't have any particular information or complaints regarding the conditions of detention and his personal and mental state at that time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [No Interpretation] THE APPELLANT: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English? Can you hear the English interpretation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hear that there was no English interpretation for that last portion. I was having Mr. Simic whether he has anything to add to what he has already said. So could we have your answer again please, Mr. Simic. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I have nothing further to add, Your Honour, to what my lawyer has already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated. Now we have -- at this Status Conference, all we can say now is that the accused has become formally the appellant in this appeal case. And, Mr. Simic, I would like to inform you in that respect that your appeal, the appellant brief, is expected within a 30-day deadline after you have received a copy of the judgement in your own language, that is to say in the B/C/S. The Registrar of the International Tribunal has informed the Chamber that the translation will be available in approximate -- or rather, by the 23rd of April, roughly. And I would like to stress, also in that regard, that another motion was filed by Franko Simatovic and that is before this Chamber and is awaiting a ruling. And Franko Simatovic has asked access to the transcripts of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Trial Chamber II, the exhibits, the other documents, and the requests that the parties made in the Bosanski Samac case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It appears that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen has the floor. It would appear that we're having difficulties again with the interpretation. So this is a technical issue. I hope we're going to be able to resolve it straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I just wanted to follow up on what my learned colleague said about the discussion that the Defence and the Prosecution had regarding disclosure earlier on this afternoon. So, Your Honours are apprised of the contents of that agreement. The parties have agreed that the Prosecution will carry out a search in the evidence collections relevant to this case, as we normally do. As you're aware, there is a disclosure suite being set up in which a number of documents will be transferred so that the Defence themselves can carry out searches in all this material. The material relevant to this case is not yet in a state where it can be put on to that system. So the Prosecution will do a search the way we normally carry out the searches. We will then sort through the documents that are the result of our searches, so as relevant -- so as to identify the documents that are relevant to the present case. As the Defence has asked for reciprocal disclosure under Rule 66 (B) in this case, the material that is generated in this way will obviously include material that falls within Rule 66 -- sorry, Rule 68. And we have therefore agreed with the Defence that we will try to sort the material out so that we are in a position to present to the Defence all relevant material. And then the Defence is satisfied that if we provide this material to the Defence, that constitutes disclosure under Rule 66 (B) as well as Rule 68. So that's the contents of the agreement we reached today. I would also like to inform the Court that we expect to be able to make this disclosure to the Defence within the next three to four weeks. I think that is all there is to say about what we have discussed today, just so Your Honour is apprised of that. If you have any questions, we are of course available. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. As the Defence said, the contacts -- your mutual contacts are underway, and I am happy to hear that the contacts have been productive and constructive, which in the long-term can ensure the speeding up of the proceedings as well as the speedier -- a speedier proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. As a matter of clarity, maybe my learned friend Mr. Marcussen was not precise with a small detail. In fact, just for the record, I would like to inform you that during the trial phase on behalf of Dr. Simic, his Defence team did not invoke 66 (B) Rule, reciprocal disclosure. So at that time, we don't think that anything should be changed with our position. We are now focused only on possible materials regarding the Rule 68. And with that regard, we shall do our best with the technical possibilities that we have in our disposal. Of course we shall be in close contact with our learned friends from the Prosecution. The reason why the position of the Defence is, as I stressed with regard to 66 (B), is very simple. During the long-lasting trial, which was -- lasted more than 200 court days, both parties actually presented more than 2.000 exhibits and thousands and thousands of pages of exhibits. So frankly, at this stage, although you never know in criminal proceedings what might arise at one time, at this stage Defence is not in possession of any particular document or exhibit. Of course, if during our search or our activity in appeal stage we will be able to come to certain relevant exhibits or documents, we shall invoke our rights from Rule 115, and accordingly we shall address the trial -- the Appeals Chamber as well as the Office of the Prosecution. So as I said, just for the record the Defence is only focused on Rule 68, and not any kind of obligations with regard to Rule 66 (B). This is a minor matter, so it's just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir. Do you have anything to add on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... with the Defence as to how we're going to do the disclosure will satisfy their needs. And if there's anything that comes up, I'm sure we can resolve it between us. I don't think there's any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We've also noticed that -- this is in the transcript, all of your remarks, and I'm satisfied to hear that there's no major difficulties between the parties in these proceedings. Since there are no motions by any party, in the absence of these motions I do not have any questions for the parties at this stage of the appeals process. But regardless of that, I would once again like to ask the parties whether they have any remarks or any other questions which they would like to initiate now. Mr. Marcussen go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. At this stage we don't have any particular matters to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since there are no other matters that need to be dealt with, this Status Conference can now be concluded. The decision has been made and the Status Conference is concluded. Thank you. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 2.35 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
